### S-456 — Malta Financial Services Authority (MFSA) (2026), "ESMA European Common Enforcement Priorities for 2026 Annual Financial Reports and Publication of the 31st FRWG (EECS) Extract of Enforcement Decisions" (Circular, 19 October 2026)
URL: https://www.mfsa.mt/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/ESMA-European-Common-Enforcement-Priorities-for-2026-Annual-Financial-Reports-and-Publication-of-the-31st-FRWG-EECS-Extract-of-Enforcement-Decisions.pdf
- **Type:** **Primary national-supervisor material** (a circular issued by a national competent authority to listed issuers in Malta), reproducing and giving national effect to ESMA's 2026 European Common Enforcement Priorities statement.
- **Supports (for IDEA-011 and gap G-33):** that the ESMA 2026 ECEP is **given effect by national enforcers, not merely published** — the register's "supervised rather than aspirational" reading, now evidenced on a second, independent supervisor's own words rather than on ESMA's alone. Read from the circular's own text: "The Authority would like to bring to your attention the Public Statement on the European Common Enforcement Priorities ('ECEP') for the 2026 Annual Financial Reports ('AFRs') of listed issuers, as published by the European Securities and Markets Authority ('ESMA') **on 13 October 2026**"; the circular sets out the ECEP's four sections (Section 1 IFRS financial statements — geopolitical risks and uncertainties, restructuring provisions and debt restructuring; Section 2 sustainability statements — materiality and the connectivity of IROs, PATs and metrics; Section 3 ESEF reporting — common errors in the statement of changes in equity; Section 4 general considerations and reminders); and, on the candidate's own limb, in the circular's Section 4: "**The implementation of IFRS 18 Presentation and Disclosure in Financial Statements, which becomes effective for annual reporting periods beginning on or after 1 January 2027 and requires comparative information for the preceding period. On this basis, in the 2026 AFR, issuers should provide the entity-specific expected impact of IFRS 18.** Consideration should be additionally made to the impact of IFRS 18 on ESEF reporting and APMs." The circular also records that "ESMA has also published the 31st Extract from the FRWG (EECS)'s Database of Enforcement containing seven enforcement decisions relating to IFRS Accounting Standards and ESMA's Guidelines on Alternative Performance Measures", that those decisions relate to "Transfer of control in bill-and-hold arrangements; Fair value measurement of a stadium; Climate-related disclosures; Capitalisation of borrowing costs relating to general borrowings; and Disclosures regarding deferred tax assets and government assistance" plus two APM fair-review decisions, and the standing commitment: "**ESMA and European NCAs will consider the matters highlighted in ESMA's Public Statement when conducting supervisory and monitoring activities relating to 2026 annual financial reports.**"
- **Why it matters for the register:** two things, both narrow. (i) It is the **second, independent line-verified carrier** of the ESMA statement's content, and it is a **national enforcer's** own expectation — which converts "supervised" from an EU-level statement into a **jurisdiction-level supervisory expectation** that an issuer must act on, and therefore strengthens the candidate's second hard-stop limb without supplying anything about a price response. (ii) It names **two dated, published supervisory objects** that the register did not previously hold: the **31st FRWG (EECS) extract of enforcement decisions** and ESMA's own undertaking to "report on their findings" of the 2026 AFR examinations. **Neither is a population rate**, so **G-33 stays open**; but both are now *named routes* to the rate, which is a change in the gap's status from "externally constrained" to "externally constrained, with two dated published routes". **No score moves** (IDEA-011 stays 69.0, rank 1): the register's standing rule is that a cell moves on evidence about the **mechanism**, not about disclosure practice.
- **Caveats:** **Malta only** — it is a national implementation of an EU-level statement, not the ESMA-supervised population rate the G-33 limb asks for, and the register records it as a **carrier and a jurisdictional-effect** fact, not as a measurement. It contains **no rate, no count and no sample** of issuers' disclosure behaviour; the "seven enforcement decisions" are a count of *published enforcement decisions*, which is a different object from a disclosure incidence rate, and the register does not use it as one. It is dated **19 October 2026** and therefore precedes the 2027 annual reporting season, so it describes no realised disclosure outcome. The circular is a **summary** of the ESMA statement, not the statement itself — the statement's own verbatim wording is carried by S-455.

### S-457 — Further national competent authority carriers of the 2026 ECEP: the CSSF (Luxembourg) document page and the Národná banka Slovenska (Slovakia) legislative-changes page (both dated 13 October 2026 for the underlying ESMA publication) — **composite entry, two carriers**
URLs: https://www.cssf.lu/en/Document/esma-public-statement-european-common-enforcement-priorities-for-2026-corporate-reporting/ · https://nbs.sk/en/financial-market-supervision1/supervision/securities-market/issuers-of-securities-basic-information/legislative-changes-and-news/
- **Type:** **Primary national-supervisor web publications** (two carriers, one per authority, bundled in one identifier and labelled as a composite, as the register's own composite convention requires). Neither is a measurement.
- **Supports (for IDEA-011 and gap G-33):** that the 2026 ECEP was **received and republished by at least two further national enforcers** on the day of its publication, which is evidence for the "supervised" reading and for the *breadth* of the supervision (the ECEP is an EEA-wide instrument, not an ESMA-only document); and, from the Slovakian authority's page, three dated facts about the **machine-readable carrier** of the IFRS 18 disclosure. Read from the carriers' own text: the **CSSF** page lists, under the title "ESMA Public Statement 'European common enforcement priorities for 2026 corporate reporting'" dated **13 October 2026**, alongside the same series for 2025, 2024, 2023, 2020, 2019 and 2018 — i.e. the Luxembourg enforcer's standing document library for the ECEP series. The **NBS** page records: "On 13 October 2026, ESMA published information on the European Common Enforcement Priorities (ECEP) for 2026. ECEP 2026 focus on geopolitical risks, restructuring provisions and debt restructuring in IFRS financial statements, materiality assessments and the connectivity of information in sustainability statements prepared under the ESRS, as well as common tagging errors in the statement of changes in equity within ESEF reporting. ESMA has also published an [extract] from its enforcement decisions database, containing seven decisions…"; and, on the taxonomy: the **ESEF RTS amendment including the 2025 IFRS taxonomy update "reflects the latest developments in international financial reporting, including the introduction of IFRS 18 and IFRS 19. The 2025 taxonomy will become mandatory for annual financial reports covering financial years starting on or after 1 January 2026. Issuers will have the possibility to apply it volun[tarily early]"**; that the RTS amendment "to include the 2025 update of the International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) taxonomy… was published in the Official Journal of the European Union"; and that "**ESMA does not plan to amend the ESEF RTS or taxonomy in 2026. This follows the IFRS Foundation's decision not to issue a 2026 IFRS Accounting Taxonomy.**"
- **Why it matters for the register:** the taxonomy facts bear **directly on G-33's route structure**, and the register records them narrowly. The **XBRL/ESEF carrier for IFRS 18 already exists** (the 2025 taxonomy carries separate IAS 1 and IFRS 18 entry points and is mandatory for financial years beginning on or after 1 January 2026), and **no further taxonomy change is planned for 2026** — so the *tagging infrastructure* for the mandated pre-adoption disclosure is settled and is not the binding constraint on a population rate. That opens a **second, independent route to the rate** for the validation stage: the **rate of IFRS 18 entry-point tagging in the filed 2026 annual financial reports** could be computed from the filings themselves, as a **proxy for the disclosure rate** (and a **upper bound** on it, because the IAS 8 expected-impact disclosure is narrative text and need not be tagged at all). **The register does not compute it, and does not acquire any filing data** — this is recorded as a **route to be handed to the validation stage**, precisely as the scope boundary requires. **No score moves**: a tagging rate would be a *proxy* for a disclosure rate, and the register's G-33 limb asks for the disclosure rate itself, so the limb **stays open** and the route is recorded as a **secondary** one.
- **Caveats:** neither carrier is a measurement; both are **listings and summaries**. The NBS page is a **narrative summary** of ESMA's publications written by a national central bank for its supervised market, not a supervisory examination finding, and its ESEP/RTS statements describe the *reporting infrastructure* and say nothing about any issuer's actual disclosure practice. The **tagging rate is a proxy, not the rate**: an issuer may disclose the expected impact in narrative form with no IFRS 18 entry-point tagging at all, so the tagging rate can be **strictly below** the disclosure rate, and it may also be below it for reasons unrelated to compliance. No price response is claimed for any of it.
- **Verification:** both carriers fetched directly on 21 October 2026 — the CSSF page **HTTP 200, text/html, 96,172 bytes** and the NBS page **HTTP 200, text/html, 122,475 bytes**; the passages above are read in each page's own visible text after script and style content was stripped. Label: **line-verified (fetched directly and read) — composite entry, two carriers**.
